entries.title: How can an animal leave a fossil without leaving a bone?
entries.answer: A track in soft mud can fill in with sand. Later, the mud and sand can harden into rock. When some of that rock breaks away, it may reveal an imprint or a raised copy of the track. A trace fossil records something an animal did instead of preserving its body. Tracks can show how many feet used to touch the ground, how big they were, and whether more than one animal walked through the same place.
facts: Burrows, feeding marks, and footprints can all be trace fossils.
A row of related footprints is called a trackway.

entries.title: How did Allosaurus bite its food?
entries.answer: Allosaurus was a big predator during the Jurassic Period. Its teeth curved backward and had tiny notches along the edges. The teeth could grip pieces of food while the edges helped cut through them. Short ridges of bone stood above the eyes. Allosaurus walked on powerful back legs, with its tail stretched behind it. It lived alongside large plant eaters, including Stegosaurus. Fossil skeletons and bite marks are among the clues that help scientists work out what it ate.
facts: Many Allosaurus fossils have been found in the western United States.
Allosaurus did not live at the same time as Tyrannosaurus rex.

questions.text: What features did another large hunter have much later?

What giant animal shared the Jurassic landscape with Allosaurus?

entries.title: How did Brachiosaurus reach high leaves?
entries.answer: Brachiosaurus had long front legs that lifted its shoulders higher than its hips. From that sloping body, a long neck reached upward, so the animal could have gathered leaves well above the height most dinosaurs could reach. Its small head had teeth suited to taking pieces from plants. Even with an unusual shape, its four thick legs supported it on land. Its name means arm lizard because its front legs are such an obvious feature.
facts: The known fossils come from the western United States.
Brachiosaurus belonged to the long-necked dinosaur group called sauropods.

questions.text: Which other sauropod had a different body shape and a very long tail?
What other plant eater lived in the same broad time and area?
How do living reptiles differ from giant plant-eating dinosaurs?

entries.title: How large was a real Velociraptor?
entries.answer: Velociraptor was about as long as an adult human lying down, but much of that length was its tail. It was shorter and lighter than many movie raptors. A curved claw on the second toe of each foot could help it hold small prey. Marks on a fossil forearm are evidence that feathers grew there. Velociraptor ran on two legs and lived in what is now central Asia, where fossils preserve one caught alongside a Protoceratops.
facts: On each back foot, one large curved claw stood out.
A famous fossil shows Velociraptor and Protoceratops together.

questions.text: Which relative of Velociraptor grew larger?
What was the dinosaur found alongside a Velociraptor like?
What do feathers tell us about the history of dinosaurs?

entries.title: How living things change over generations
entries.answer: Living things often have small differences from others of the same kind. Suppose some beetles have a color that makes it harder for birds to spot them. If young beetles can inherit that color and beetles with it tend to have more young, the helpful color may become more common in later generations. That is one way evolution can happen. Evolution is change in a group over generations. It does not mean one beetle changes its kind while it grows up. Changes can build up in a group over a long time.

sections.heading: What is an adaptation?
sections.text: An adaptation is a feature that helps living things survive or have young in the place where they live. A feature that helps in one place might make less difference somewhere else.

facts: Natural selection is one way evolution can happen.
Fossils are some of the evidence scientists use to study evolution.

entries.title: How was Ankylosaurus armored?
entries.answer: Ankylosaurus was a low, wide dinosaur that ate plants. Like the hard covering on a turtle, rows of bony plates helped protect it. Its plates were set into skin across much of its back and neck. Its tail ended in a large lump of bone that could have worked like a club. A powerful swing might have made it difficult for a hunter to get near. An opening at the front of its jaws formed a beak for cropping leaves.
facts: Ankylosaurus supported its heavy body on four legs.
The tail club was not one single round bone.

questions.text: How was a tail with spikes different from a tail club?
Which similarly heavy plant eater wore horns on its head?
Which large hunter lived in the same time and part of the world?

entries.title: Tyrannosaurus rex
entries.answer: Tyrannosaurus rex was a large dinosaur that walked on two back legs. Some adults reached about 40 feet long. A long tail helped balance the weight of the big head and body. Its thick teeth and strong jaws could crush bone, which helps scientists work out what it could eat. The two short arms each ended in two clawed fingers. Its fossils come from western North America. T. rex lived near the end of the time when large dinosaurs walked the land.
facts: T. rex means ‘tyrant lizard king.’
Tyrannosaurus rex lived toward the end of the Cretaceous Period.

entries.title: Was Oviraptor really an egg thief?
entries.answer: When an Oviraptor skeleton was found on a nest, researchers first thought the animal had been trying to eat another dinosaur’s eggs. Its name means egg thief. Years later, a fossil baby inside a matching kind of egg showed that eggs of that shape belonged to an Oviraptor relative. The adult on the nest may have been guarding or warming eggs. One new clue can change a good story about the past without requiring a change to the name.
facts: Oviraptor walked on two legs and had a beak.

questions.text: Which dinosaur was first thought to have made those eggs?
What was unusual about another dinosaur fossil discovered in Asia?
How can a new fossil change an older explanation?

entries.title: Were pterosaurs flying dinosaurs?
entries.answer: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles that lived while many dinosaurs walked on land. Their wings stretched between their bodies and one very long finger on each hand. They had no feathered wing like a bird. Some were small and probably ate insects, while others reached the length of a small aircraft from wingtip to wingtip. Fossil wings and footprints show that some pterosaurs also walked on four limbs when they were on the ground.
facts: Pterosaurs belonged to a separate branch from dinosaurs.
They were the first known animals with backbones to achieve powered flight.

entries.title: What can fossil poop tell us?
entries.answer: A coprolite is a dropping that became a fossil. While an animal’s body tells us what the animal looked like, what it left behind may tell us something about how it lived. A researcher might find a fish scale, a piece of bone, or a bit of plant trapped inside. Those pieces are clues to what the animal ate. Since different animals may leave similar droppings, figuring out which one made a fossil can be much harder.
facts: A coprolite is a kind of trace fossil.
Some fossil droppings preserve tiny fragments that are easier to see under a microscope.

entries.title: What could a Parasaurolophus crest do?
entries.answer: Parasaurolophus had a long hollow crest that swept back from the top of its head. The crest contained connected passages from its nose. Air moving through the passages might have changed the sound the animal could make, somewhat like the way a long musical instrument can change a note. The crest also shaped its outline and may have helped other dinosaurs recognize it. A beak and rows of teeth let Parasaurolophus gather and chew plants.
facts: Parasaurolophus could move on two feet or all four.
Its crest could have had more than one use.

How can air carry a sound?

entries.title: What did an early little dinosaur look like?
entries.answer: Coelophysis was a lightly built dinosaur with a long neck and tail and small, sharp teeth. It walked and ran on its hind legs. Its legs were slender, giving it a very different shape from the huge four-legged plant eaters that appeared later. It lived during the Triassic Period, early in the age of dinosaurs. A fossil site in New Mexico holds the remains of many Coelophysis individuals in the same area, allowing researchers to compare their sizes and bones.
facts: The name Coelophysis refers to its hollow bones.

questions.text: How was a later, much larger dinosaur built differently?

How can a track tell us that a dinosaur moved on two feet?

entries.title: What did Protoceratops look like?
entries.answer: Protoceratops was a compact plant-eating dinosaur with a beak and a wide frill at the back of its head. It did not have the long horns of the later Triceratops. Scientists have found many Protoceratops fossils in rocks from Asia, including some belonging to young animals. One famous find held a Protoceratops near the bones of a Velociraptor, with the two bodies close together. That fossil provides an unusual clue about how dinosaurs sometimes met.
facts: Protoceratops was much smaller than Triceratops.
A hard beak helped it gather plants.

questions.text: How do the skulls of Protoceratops and Triceratops differ?

Why were some dinosaur eggs once wrongly blamed on an egg thief?

entries.title: What fossils tell us
entries.answer: A fossil is something from long-ago life that lasts into the present. It might be part of a shell or a tooth, or a mark left by a leaf or a walking animal. Fossils can form when sand or mud quickly covers a body or a mark and protects it. Over time, the layers may harden into rock. A footprint can show how an animal walked, even if no bones of that animal were found nearby. Scientists look at fossils and the rocks around them to learn about life long before people kept records.
facts: Bones and shells are often better preserved than soft body parts.
A dinosaur track can be a fossil even though it is not a piece of the dinosaur.

questions.text: How do mud and sand become layers of rock?
What can a huge tooth tell us about Tyrannosaurus rex?
How do fossils help show that living things change over time?

entries.title: What happened to most dinosaurs
entries.answer: About 66 million years ago, most kinds of dinosaurs disappeared. Scientists have strong evidence that a huge asteroid hit Earth at about that time. The impact left a wide crater near what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. Dust and other material from the crash spread through the air and reduced the sunlight that reached the ground. That made it harder for plants to grow and broke up the food supply of many animals. Some living things survived, including ancestors of the birds we see today.
facts: A thin layer of rock in many places contains signs of the impact.
All dinosaurs outside the bird branch died out.

entries.title: What helped woolly mammoths live in the cold?
entries.answer: A woolly mammoth had a shaggy coat over much of its body. Smaller ears than many living elephants also helped reduce heat loss. Its long, curved tusks could have helped push snow aside to reach plants, among other uses. Woolly mammoths lived much later than most dinosaurs. Some bodies froze in cold ground and kept their hair, skin, or stomach contents. Those finds give clues a normal fossil made only of bone cannot provide.
facts: Some woolly mammoth remains have been preserved in Alaska and Siberia.
Mammoths and modern elephants are relatives.

questions.text: How do the bodies of living elephants compare with mammoths?
What happened long before mammoths lived?
How can moving masses of ice change land during a cold period?

entries.title: What is the tall sail on a Spinosaurus?
entries.answer: Spinosaurus had very tall bones projecting from its spine. Together they supported a sail-like rise above its back. Its jaws were long, with pointed teeth shaped a little like cones, which fit well for catching slippery food like fish. Fossils suggest it spent time around water, but scientists still discuss exactly how it moved and hunted there. Spinosaurus lived in northern Africa at a time when large river systems covered places that are much drier today.
facts: Some Spinosaurus fossils were discovered in Egypt and Morocco.
Spinosaurus teeth have a different shape from the cutting teeth of many large hunters.

questions.text: How did another large meat eater’s teeth work?
Which huge predator lived much later in western North America?
What records other than bones can tell scientists about an animal’s behavior?

entries.title: What lived inside an ammonite shell?
entries.answer: Many ammonites left fossils that look like stone spirals. In life, an ammonite was a sea animal related to squids and octopuses, and the shell held its soft body. As it grew, it added new parts to the shell, sealing off older rooms behind it. Ammonites evolved many different shell shapes. Their fossils help researchers compare the ages of rocks, since some distinct kinds were common for only a short part of Earth’s past.
facts: Ammonites lived in the ocean.
Many shells were coiled, but some ammonites had straighter or oddly curved shells.

questions.text: How does a living ocean animal use several shell chambers?
Which other animal left ancient shells in the rocks?
What happened to ammonites around the time most dinosaurs vanished?

entries.title: What was a trilobite?
entries.answer: A trilobite was a small ocean animal related to today’s insects, spiders, and crabs. Its outer shell was divided along its length into a center section and two side sections. The three parts give trilobites their name. Many had eyes and short legs underneath, though the soft parts are much harder to find in fossils. As a trilobite grew, it sometimes left its old shell behind. Trilobites lived for a span of time much longer than dinosaurs later did.
facts: Trilobites lived in ancient seas.
Some trilobites could roll into a ball.

questions.text: Which other old ocean animals left many hard shells?

What later event ended the time of most dinosaurs?

entries.title: What was the thick dome on Pachycephalosaurus?
entries.answer: Pachycephalosaurus walked on two legs and had an unusually thick dome of bone on top of its skull. Smaller bony bumps surrounded part of the head. The dome might have helped the animals push or bump each other during contests, or it might have made them easier to recognize. Scientists compare several kinds of evidence before choosing among these ideas. Many of the fossils found are fragments of skull, telling much more about the head than the rest of the animal.
facts: Pachycephalosaurus means thick-headed lizard.
Its skull dome was solid bone.

questions.text: Which dinosaur had air passages in its head crest instead?
What other large bones could rise above a dinosaur’s face?
Why can a fossil tell us much more about one body part than another?

entries.title: What were the three horns of Triceratops for?
entries.answer: Triceratops walked on four legs and ate plants. Two long horns rose above its eyes, and it had a smaller horn over its nose. A bony frill spread out from the back of its skull. The horns and frill could have been useful for protection, display, or contests with other Triceratops. Scientists look at skulls for signs of damage and at how these structures changed as the animal grew to learn how it might have used them.
facts: Triceratops had a hard beak at the front of its mouth.
It lived in western North America toward the end of the age of most dinosaurs.

questions.text: How does a smaller dinosaur with a frill differ from Triceratops?
Which plant eater had thick armor all along its back?

entries.title: Why birds are living dinosaurs
entries.answer: Birds belong to one branch of the dinosaur family. Their early relatives were small, two-legged dinosaurs that lived long before people. Scientists see clues to that family link in fossils. Some dinosaurs that were not birds had feathers. Some also had bones or feet that share details with those of early birds. This does not mean a chicken came directly from Tyrannosaurus rex. Birds and T. rex are more like distant cousins, and their family branches go back to an older group of meat-eating dinosaurs.
facts: Some dinosaur feathers existed before birds could fly.
The bird branch survived after the other dinosaur branches died out.

entries.title: Why did Diplodocus have such a long tail?
entries.answer: Diplodocus was a long-necked dinosaur with a tail that narrowed to a thin tip. The tail alone made up a large part of its length. It may have helped the animal balance, send signals, or defend itself. Diplodocus gathered plant material with narrow teeth grouped near the front of its mouth. It did not have the broad grinding teeth people use to chew. Keeping its feet in one spot, it could reach plants over a wide area.
facts: Diplodocus walked on four legs and supported a long neck.
Fossils show that it lived in what is now western North America.

entries.title: Why did Iguanodon have a spike on its thumb?
entries.answer: One finger on an Iguanodon hand ended in an unusual spike. Some early researchers put the spike on the dinosaur’s nose because they had only scattered fossils to work with. More complete hands showed where it belonged. The spike may have helped with defense. Iguanodon gathered plants with its beak and used rows of teeth farther back to cut plant material. It could move on two legs or on all fours.
facts: Iguanodon’s name refers to the shape of its teeth.

questions.text: How did a relative chew plants with a long row of teeth?
What kind of defense did a different four-legged dinosaur have?
Why can a more complete skeleton change an earlier guess?

entries.title: Why did Stegosaurus have plates down its back?
entries.answer: Two rows of tall plates stood along the back of Stegosaurus. The plates were made of bone, but sat in the skin rather than joining the backbone. They could have made the animal look bigger or helped other stegosauruses see it. Scientists are still working out their uses. Four pointed spikes near the end of the tail were different. The animal could swing its tail, so these spikes may have helped defend it against a predator.
facts: Stegosaurus ate plants and walked on four legs.
Its head was small compared with the rest of its body.

questions.text: Which other dinosaur had a heavy club at the end of its tail?
Which large hunter lived around the same time as Stegosaurus?
How were horns and a frill arranged on a different dinosaur?

entries.title: Why does Archaeopteryx look like both a bird and a dinosaur?
entries.answer: An Archaeopteryx fossil can show feather marks beside the bones. The long feathers on the wings look much like some bird feathers today. The animal also had teeth, claws on its wings, and a long tail made of bone. These are features found in earlier dinosaurs related to birds. The mix of old and new features helped scientists understand how birds fit into the dinosaur family. Fossils from fine limestone in Germany preserve the outline of many of its feathers.
facts: Archaeopteryx was about the size of a modern raven, depending on the specimen.
Its fossil specimens are from the Late Jurassic.

questions.text: Why do scientists consider modern birds part of the dinosaur group?
What other kind of dinosaur had feathers on its arms?
How did a pterosaur wing differ from a feathered wing?

entries.title: Why is Deinonychus called a terrible claw?
entries.answer: Deinonychus had a large, sharply curved claw on one toe of each foot. Its name means terrible claw. The rest of its body included long arms and a tail that could help keep it balanced when it moved. Studying this dinosaur helped researchers rethink the idea that all dinosaurs were slow. Its bones suggested an active animal that could run on two feet. Deinonychus was related to Velociraptor, but its body was longer and heavier.
facts: Deinonychus fossils have been found in North America.
Its back teeth curved backward.
